name: com.customsolutionsindy/custom-solutions
title: Custom Solutions
description: Real estate and employee turnover calculators and an AI visibility check, from Custom Solutions.

tools.name: search_answers
tools.description: Full-text search over Custom Solutions' published answer pages and blog notes. Returns up to 10 matches with title, summary and canonical URL.

tools.name: get_answer
tools.description: Full text of one published answer page (or blog note) by slug, with its FAQ and canonical URL.

tools.name: get_services
tools.description: The nine parts of the Custom Solutions digital-services offer (private AI knowledge system, AEO, MCP server, managed websites), with short and long descriptions. Prices are not published; pricing is quoted per engagement.

tools.name: get_service_area
tools.description: The Central Indiana counties and cities Custom Solutions works in (in person), with how to reach it.

tools.name: get_company_facts
tools.description: Name, address, phone, email, hours, cities served, what the company does, how an engagement runs, and its one-company-per-industry exclusivity policy, in plain words.

tools.name: compute_noi
tools.description: Net operating income (NOI) of a rental property per year: scheduled rent less vacancy, management, maintenance, capital reserve and fixed costs, before any mortgage payment. NOI is easy to overstate: management is charged on rent actually collected, maintenance and reserves on scheduled rent, and the debt payment is left out entirely, so a figure that subtracts the mortgage is cash flow instead. Send the monthly rent for the whole property; vacancy, management, maintenance and capex as percents (8 means 8%); and the yearly fixed costs (tax, insurance, owner-paid utilities, HOA). Any omitted expense counts as 0 and is listed in the answer's inputs.

monthly_rent.description: Scheduled rent for the whole property per month, in dollars, e.g. 2400

other_income_monthly.description: Laundry, parking or pet income per month, e.g. 50

vacancy_pct.description: Vacancy and credit loss as a percent of rent, e.g. 8 for 8%

management_pct.description: Property management as a percent of collected rent, e.g. 8

maintenance_pct.description: Repairs and maintenance as a percent of scheduled rent, e.g. 8

capex_pct.description: Capital reserve as a percent of scheduled rent, e.g. 5

annual_fixed_costs.description: Property tax, insurance, owner-paid utilities, HOA and other fixed costs per year, e.g. 5400

tools.name: compute_cap_rate
tools.description: Capitalization rate of a property: yearly NOI divided by the purchase price, as a ratio and a percent, with the most to pay for a target cap rate and the monthly rent-to-price ratio when those inputs are sent. A cap rate is only as good as its NOI: a monthly figure sent as yearly, or NOI after the mortgage, gives a number that looks plausible and is wrong by a factor of twelve or more, so the answer flags a cap rate over 25% and rent over 3% of price. Send noi (per year, may be negative) and price; optionally target_cap_pct and monthly_rent. A price of 0 is refused by name.

noi.description: Net operating income per year, in dollars, e.g. 28000

target_cap_pct.description: Target cap rate in percent, e.g. 8, for the most to pay at that rate

monthly_rent.description: Scheduled rent per month, e.g. 3200, for the rent-to-price ratio

tools.name: compute_cash_on_cash
tools.description: Cash-on-cash return of a rental: yearly cash flow after principal and interest divided by the cash put into the deal, with the payback period in years. The hard part is the denominator: cash invested is the down payment plus closing costs, points, lender fees and repairs paid in cash, and leaving any of them out inflates the return. Send annual_cash_flow (after the mortgage, negative when the property loses money) and cash_invested. A negative cash flow is computed and flagged rather than refused; the payback period is null when cash flow is not positive.

annual_cash_flow.description: Cash flow per year after the mortgage, e.g. 6000 (negative when it loses money)

cash_invested.description: Cash put in: down payment, closing costs, points, repairs paid in cash, e.g. 80000

tools.name: compute_dscr
tools.description: Debt service coverage ratio of a rental, two ways: NOI divided by yearly principal and interest, and the figure DSCR-loan lenders use on 1-4 unit rentals, scheduled rent divided by PITIA (payment plus tax, insurance and HOA). The two definitions give different numbers for the same property, which is why quotes of a DSCR often disagree; both are labelled in the answer. With target_dscr, rate_pct and amort_years the answer also sizes the largest loan the NOI supports. Send noi and annual_debt_service, plus gross_rent_annual, annual_tax, annual_insurance and annual_hoa for the lender figure. Zero debt service is refused: with no debt, DSCR does not exist.

noi.description: Net operating income per year, e.g. 28000

annual_debt_service.description: Principal and interest paid per year, e.g. 22000

gross_rent_annual.description: Scheduled rent per year, e.g. 38400, for the lender rent-to-PITIA figure

annual_tax.description: Property tax per year, e.g. 3600, for the lender figure

annual_insurance.description: Insurance per year, e.g. 1800, for the lender figure

annual_hoa.description: HOA dues per year, e.g. 0, for the lender figure

target_dscr.description: Lender minimum DSCR, e.g. 1.25, to size the largest loan

rate_pct.description: Loan interest rate in percent, e.g. 7.25, for the largest loan

amort_years.description: Amortization in years, e.g. 30, for the largest loan

tools.name: compute_mortgage_payment
tools.description: Monthly principal and interest on a loan, the payment in year 1 when the loan starts interest-only, the debt service over the first 12 months and per year, and the cost of points. Payment figures differ with compounding and with how interest-only months are handled: this engine compounds monthly, pays at the end of each month and, after an interest-only period, amortizes over the full term as the Analyzer workbook does; each convention is stated in the answer. Send loan_amount, rate_pct (7.25 means 7.25% a year) and amort_years (0 means interest-only); optionally io_months and points_pct. A rate over 30% a year is refused as a likely typo.

rate_pct.description: Interest rate in percent per year, e.g. 7.25

amort_years.description: Amortization in years, e.g. 30; 0 means interest-only

io_months.description: Interest-only months at the start, e.g. 12

points_pct.description: Points as a percent of the loan, e.g. 1

tools.name: compute_amortization
tools.description: Amortization schedule of a loan: interest, principal and ending balance for each year, and the balance left after a chosen year, which is the payoff figure behind a refinance or a sale. Balances drift when a schedule mixes yearly and monthly compounding or skips interest-only months; this one sums the monthly schedule and holds principal at zero during interest-only months. Send loan_amount, rate_pct and amort_years (1 to 40); optionally io_months and year. The schedule covers the whole term.

rate_pct.description: Interest rate in percent per year, e.g. 7.25

io_months.description: Interest-only months at the start, e.g. 12

year.description: Year whose ending balance to report, e.g. 7

tools.name: compute_break_even_occupancy
tools.description: Break-even occupancy of a rental: the share of scheduled rent needed to pay operating expenses and debt service, and the cushion left above it. Over 100% means the property cannot cover its costs even fully rented. The common mistake is measuring against collected rent instead of scheduled rent, which hides the vacancy the figure exists to show. Send gross_rent_annual (scheduled rent at full occupancy), operating_expenses_annual and, when there is a loan, annual_debt_service; with no debt service the figure covers operating expenses only.

gross_rent_annual.description: Scheduled rent per year at full occupancy, e.g. 36000

annual_debt_service.description: Principal and interest per year, e.g. 12000 (0 for no loan)

tools.name: compute_max_offer_at_cap_rate
tools.description: Most to pay for a rental so its NOI earns a target cap rate: NOI divided by the target, less the repairs and purchase costs the deal needs, with a floor of 0. Working backward from a cap rate is where offers go wrong, because the value at the target cap rate still has to pay for repairs and closing costs before it becomes a price. Send the stabilized yearly noi and target_cap_pct (8 means 8%); optionally repairs and purchase_costs. A negative NOI gives a maximum price of 0 with a flag.

target_cap_pct.description: Target cap rate in percent, e.g. 8

purchase_costs.description: Closing, inspection and other purchase costs, e.g. 4000

tools.name: compute_flip_profit
tools.description: Profit on a buy, fix and sell: the net sale after selling costs, less price, purchase costs, repairs, holding costs and points, with the cash needed, the return on that cash and, with min_profit_pct, the most to pay and still keep that profit. Holding costs are what most flip estimates miss: interest on an interest-only loan plus tax, insurance and utilities for every month held, with months rounded up. Send price, arv, repairs, months and selling_costs_pct; optionally purchase_costs, holding_costs_monthly, loan_pct_of_price, loan_pct_of_repairs, rate_pct, points_pct and min_profit_pct. Omitted loan inputs mean an all-cash flip.

repairs.description: All repairs plus resale prep, e.g. 45000

months.description: Months to finish and sell, e.g. 5 (rounded up, at least 1)

selling_costs_pct.description: Selling costs as a percent of the sale price, e.g. 7

purchase_costs.description: Closing and other purchase costs, e.g. 3500

holding_costs_monthly.description: Tax, insurance and utilities per month while held, e.g. 400

loan_pct_of_price.description: Share of the price the lender funds, in percent, e.g. 85

loan_pct_of_repairs.description: Share of repairs the lender funds, in percent, e.g. 100

points_pct.description: Points as a percent of the loan, e.g. 2

min_profit_pct.description: Minimum profit as a percent of ARV, e.g. 12, for the most to pay

tools.name: compare_rental_vs_flip
tools.description: Whether a property earns more as a rental held for a number of years or as a flip: the rental's total profit (cash flow over the hold plus sale proceeds after selling costs and the loan payoff, less the cash invested) against the flip's profit, with the difference and the rental's yearly return. The comparison is only fair over the same money: the rental side needs its loan balance at sale and the growth of rent, expenses and value. Send price, noi, annual_debt_service, cash_invested, hold_years and flip_profit; optionally arv, loan_amount, rate_pct, amort_years, growth_pct, value_growth_pct and selling_costs_pct. Without arv the price is grown.

annual_debt_service.description: Principal and interest per year, e.g. 9800 (0 for no loan)

cash_invested.description: Cash put into the rental, e.g. 40000

hold_years.description: Years held before selling, 1 to 30, e.g. 7

arv.description: Value after repairs, e.g. 180000; the price is used when absent

loan_amount.description: Loan amount, e.g. 120000, for the balance at sale

growth_pct.description: Yearly growth of rent and expenses in percent, e.g. 3

value_growth_pct.description: Yearly growth of the property value in percent, e.g. 3

selling_costs_pct.description: Selling costs at the end of the hold in percent, e.g. 7

tools.name: compute_irr
tools.description: Internal rate of return of a series of cash flows, per period, with the equity multiple and every rate that sets the net present value to zero. IRR is where calculators silently disagree: a series with no sign change has no IRR at all, and one that changes sign more than once can have several; this engine refuses the first with a named reason and lists every root of the second. Send cash_flows as comma-separated numbers, period 0 first, with money put in as negative numbers, for example -100000,8000,8500,9000,9500,130000. Yearly flows give a yearly IRR.

cash_flows.description: Comma-separated cash flows, period 0 first, e.g. -100000,8000,8500,9000,9500,130000

tools.name: compute_1031_deadlines
tools.description: The two deadlines of a 1031 like-kind exchange from the date the relinquished property was transferred: day 45 to identify replacement property, and the end of the exchange period, which is the earlier of day 180 or the due date (with extensions) of the tax return for the year of the transfer. Calendar arithmetic is where these go wrong: day 1 is the day after the transfer, a deadline on a weekend or holiday stays where it falls, and a late-year transfer can lose weeks to an unextended return. Send transfer_date as YYYY-MM-DD and, when day 180 may fall after the return is due, return_due_date; without it, the answer names both candidate dates and the missing input.

transfer_date.description: Date the relinquished property was transferred, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-11-19

return_due_date.description: Due date, with extensions, of the tax return for the year of the transfer, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2027-10-15

tools.name: compute_rent_raise_turnover
tools.description: Expected move-outs and year-1 cost of raising below-market rents to market, under Custom Solutions' model from its Rental Property Portfolio Analyzer: the share of current tenants likely to leave, the make-ready cost per unit that turns over and the rent lost while those units sit empty. The figure is hard to estimate because move-outs rise with the size of the raise, with month-to-month tenancies and with the length of tenancy; the model's parameters are the firm's planning assumptions, listed in the answer. Send current_rent and market_rent per unit per month and units; optionally vacant_units, month_to_month_units and tenancy_years.

current_rent.description: Average rent current tenants pay per unit per month, e.g. 1050

market_rent.description: Market rent per unit per month, e.g. 1450

month_to_month_units.description: Tenanted units with no lease, e.g. 2

tenancy_years.description: Average years the current tenants have lived there, e.g. 9

tools.name: check_ai_visibility
tools.description: Site readiness of a website for AI search, 100 points in four parts: reach (robots.txt and a live test of the crawlers of ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google, Bing and Apple), readable (text without JavaScript on the home page and up to five inner pages), understood (title, headings, business structured data, contact details) and answerable (question headings, FAQ or article markup, sitemap dates), with a fix per problem.

domain.description: Domain name (a pasted web address also works)

tools.name: calculate_employee_turnover_cost
tools.description: Employee turnover rate and turnover cost from a business's own figures. Rate: people who left divided by average headcount times 100 (the Bureau of Labor Statistics separation-rate arithmetic), annualized for a period under 12 months, each step shown. An industry code adds the 2025 Bureau of Labor Statistics separations rate, published monthly; the yearly figure is 12 times it. Cost per departure adds only the lines sent (hiring, empty-seat days, ramp-up at a productivity gap that defaults to 50%, training hours, lost-knowledge hours); no percent-of-salary rule of thumb.

separations.description: People who left in the period

industry.description: Industry code, e.g. retail or health-care; a wrong code returns the list
